title: Folded cascode OTA
description: A folded cascode: the input pair steers current into a folding node, and a cascoded output branch carries it to a high-impedance output. It is the branch-current bookkeeping showcase. The input pair evaluates FIRST at half the tail current; each folding-branch current source is biased at $I_{branch}$, and the output cascode and mirror carry the fold current $I_{fold} = I_{branch} - I_{tail}/2$ — a later child reads the earlier input device's provided current to compute its own bias. The fold current is a real design knob: it must exceed the peak steered current ($I_{tail}/2$) so the branch never starves during slew, but the folding current sources add input-referred noise, so more fold current trades noise for slew headroom. Gain is $g_{m,in}$ times the folded-cascode output resistance; unlike the telescopic it separates the input CM range from the output swing, at the cost of the extra branch current and its noise. The stack is parameterized by its NODES: the tail node is pinned so the produced $CM_{in}$ equals $CM_{dc}$, and the folding node $V_{fold}$ and the mirror-drain node $V_c$ are choice params — every device $V_{DS}$ is a subtraction between adjacent nodes and every source-above-bulk device carries its true body bias, so the drops close each branch by construction. The retired per-device estimates could not even agree on where the folding node sat; the node form makes that inconsistency inexpressible.

params.name: vn_target
params.note: input-referred thermal density budget. The folding current sources are the fold's noise price: the gamma-model total lands near 25 nV/rtHz at the default currents, well above a telescopic at the same gm — this budget leaves headroom while keeping that trade visible

params.name: vos_target
params.note: input offset budget, 1 sigma; the output mirror's spread referred through the fold puts the total near 10 mV at half-micron areas

params.name: CM_lo
params.note: input CM range the application presents, low edge — proven exactly by the cm-lo edge at every evaluation (the sweep put the widest closing range at 0.95 up to the 1.55 probe ceiling V on sky130 tt at the shipped choices). The edge proves the ENDPOINT; the interior is the sweep's to show

params.name: CM_hi
params.note: input CM range the application presents, high edge — its ENDPOINT proven by the cm-hi edge the same way

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: the input common mode the application presents. The engine places the tail node so the sheet sits exactly here; sweep it to trace the common-mode axis

params.name: V_out_dc
params.note: output DC level; the NMOS-side nodes climb to it and the folding node descends to it

params.name: V_tail
params.note: the tail node — the pair's source. Solved rather than set: bisected between min and max (the BRACKET) until the produced common mode equals CM_dc

params.name: V_fold
params.note: the folding node: input-pair drains, folding-source drain, and PMOS-cascode source in one. The input vds is V_fold - V_tail, the folding source's is VDD - V_fold, and the PMOS cascode's is V_fold - V_out_dc — by construction

params.name: V_c
params.note: the NMOS-side internal node: mirror drain and NMOS-cascode source. The mirror vds is V_c and the cascode's is V_out_dc - V_c, by construction

params.name: sign_p
params.note: vds sign convention of the PMOS-side tables: +1 for an N-style axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis

params.name: I_tail
params.note: input-pair tail current; sets gm_in and the slew current into CL

params.name: I_branch
params.note: folding-branch bias current; the fold current I_fold = I_branch - I_tail/2 must stay positive (slew headroom vs current-source noise)

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion: sets gm per current and the input-referred noise

params.name: gm_id_casc
params.note: cascode-device inversion: higher gm/ID lifts cascode gain but costs vdsat headroom

params.name: gm_id_cs
params.note: current-source and mirror inversion: lower gm/ID adds less noise and offset

doc.title: Input-pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device at half the tail current; evaluates first so the folding branch can read its current.

doc.title: Tail current source
doc.description: Carries the full bias current; its drain-source voltage IS the tail node.

doc.title: Folding current source (PMOS)
doc.description: The top current source biased at I_branch; feeds the folding node. Its ro (cascoded) sets the PMOS-side output resistance, and it adds input-referred noise.

doc.title: PMOS cascode (folded branch)
doc.description: Cascodes the folding current source; carries the fold current I_fold = I_branch - I_tail/2 read from the input device. Its av0 sets the PMOS-side cascode boost.

doc.title: NMOS cascode (output branch)
doc.description: Cascodes the NMOS mirror; carries the fold current. Its av0 sets the NMOS-side cascode boost.

doc.title: NMOS mirror (output branch)
doc.description: Bottom of the output branch; its ro (cascoded by ncasc) sets the NMOS-side output resistance, and it adds input-referred noise.

rows.name: CM_in
rows.note: the input common mode this bias produces — an OUTPUT here, not a setting; rises monotonically with the tail node, so the pin is a well-posed bisection

rows.name: tail_headroom
rows.note: how far the tail node sits above the tail device's saturation edge — exact, because the tail node is the variable rather than something inferred from a common mode

rows.name: I_fold
rows.note: the folded branch current: the branch bias minus the peak steered input current

rows.name: Rout_p
rows.note: PMOS side: the folding current source ro boosted by the PMOS-cascode gain

rows.name: Rout_n
rows.note: NMOS side: the output mirror ro boosted by the NMOS-cascode gain

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: the two cascoded sides in parallel

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: input pair plus the top and bottom current-source pairs, each at its own density; the folding sources are the price of the fold

rows.name: vos
rows.expr: sqrt(pelgrom_vos(avt, abeta, in__W, L_in, gm_id_in)^2 + (pelgrom_vos(avt, abeta, nmir__W, L_cs, gm_id_cs)*nmir__gm/in__gm)^2)
rows.note: input-pair offset plus the output-mirror offset referred by the gm ratio

rules.note: below this the tail source drops out of saturation and the bias current collapses; the mechanism behind the low end of the common-mode range
the folded branch must carry at least the peak steered current so it does not starve during slew
node placement: the folding node must sit at least a vdsat above the tail node. The branch drops close by construction — what is left to check is that each node leaves its device saturated
node placement: the folding node must leave the folding source at least a vdsat below VDD
node placement: the folding node must sit at least a vdsat above the output DC
node placement: the output DC must sit at least a vdsat above V_c
node placement: V_c must leave the mirror at least a vdsat above ground
the common mode this bias produces has to sit inside the range the application presents
paired with cm-not-below; the cm-lo/cm-hi edges prove the range ENDS close, and the CM_dc sweep shows the whole landscape

edges.name: cm-lo
edges.note: the claimed low edge, proven exactly: the whole sheet re-evaluates at CM_dc = CM_lo — its own tail-node solve from the full bracket, its own devices — and every hard rule must hold there

edges.name: cm-hi
edges.note: the claimed high edge, proven the same way. Edges prove the ENDPOINTS; the CM_dc sweep remains the authority on the full landscape
